title: Configuration Guide for Microsoft Azure AD

blocks.text: This guide provides information on how to set up Microsoft Azure Active Directory (AD) as a IdP for Private Access (ZPA).
Zscaler and Microsoft are technology partners. To learn more about integrating Zscaler and Microsoft Azure AD, see the Zscaler and Microsoft Entra ID Passwordless Deployment Guide.
Ensure that you have the following:

blocks.item: A premium Azure AD subscription, or an Azure AD subscription that has used less than 10 gallery Single Sign-On (SSO) applications with the license.
An existing directory in Azure AD.
A Private Access account with an administrator role that allows you to add an IdP Configuration.

blocks.text: The reference to private.zscaler.com in this article might differ depending on your organization’s assigned cloud. To learn more, see Customizing Your Account Settings.
To configure Azure AD as the IdP for Private Access user and admin SSO:

blocks.item: Log in to the Azure portal and go to Azure Active Directory > Enterprise applications from the left navigation pane.
See image.
Click New application.
See image.
Under Add from the gallery, search for Zscaler Private Access. Choose one of the following:
For Private Access user SSO in the IdP configuration, click the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) application.
For Private Access admin SSO in the IdP configuration, click the Zscaler Private Access Administrator application.

blocks.text: The following images in this procedure use the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) application as an example.

blocks.item: Click Add.
See image.

blocks.text: You are redirected to the Zscaler application's Overview page.

blocks.item: Click Single sign-on, then SAML.
See image.

blocks.text: The Set up Single Sign-on with SAML - Preview page appears.

blocks.item: For Basic SAML Configuration, click Edit and complete the following fields:
For Identifier (Entity ID) enter the Service Provider Entity ID that is provided for you when you configure a new IdP configuration in Zscaler Admin Console. This ID is specific to your IdP.

For Reply URL (Assertion Customer Service URL) enter the Service Provider URL that is provided for you when you configured a new IdP configuration in Zscaler Admin Console. This URL is specific to your IdP.
For Sign on URL:
View the step for Private Access user SSO configuration.
Enter the same URL you used for the Reply URL (Assertion Customer Service URL) field from step 6b.
Vew the step for Private Access admin SSO configuration.
Leave the Sign on URL field blank.
Click Save.

blocks.text: After saving, you will be prompted to test the configuration. Do not test the configuration at this time.

blocks.item: Leave User Attributes & Claims as default and skip to the next step.

Under SAML Signing Certificate, for Federation Metadata XML, click the Download link to obtain the metadata file. You will need to upload this IdP metadata information to the Zscaler Admin Console later to complete the configuration.
Leave Set up Zscaler Private Access (for Private Access user SSO) or Set up Zscaler Private Access Administrator (for Private Access admin SSO) as default, and skip to the next step.

blocks.text: Do not test the configuration at this time.

blocks.item: In order for Azure AD users to authenticate through Private Access, you must assign these users to the Private Access application. In the application, click Users and Groups then Add user.
See image.
Search for the user you want to assign to the Private Access application.
Select the checkbox next to the username, then click Select.
See image.
In the Add Assignment panel, click Assign.
See image.
If you are configuring the Azure AD for user SSO and want to use SCIM, proceed to the SCIM Configuration Guide for Microsoft Azure AD.

If you are configuring the Azure AD for user SSO, proceed to the Using Roles for Group Mapping procedure, then complete the IdP configuration. If you are configuring the Azure AD for admin SSO, you can go directly to the Zscaler Admin Console to complete the IdP configuration.

blocks.text: The following procedure applies to IdP configurations for Private Access user SSO only.
If all of the following criteria are met, then group mapping is not required:

blocks.item: User-friendly group names are only sent to Azure AD using Azure AD Connect. For example, groups from an on-premise active directory show up in Azure AD when Azure AD Connect syncs the group information.
AD Connect is on version 1.2.7.0 or greater.

blocks.text: To configure group mapping in Azure AD, you must customize the role claim type in the SAML response token in order to push groups to Private Access. To learn more about configuring role claims, see the Microsoft product documentation.

blocks.item: 1. Adding Roles in the Private Access Application
You must add a role for each group you've created. If possible, ensure that the role name and group name are the same.
To add a role in the Private Access application:
Go to Microsoft Graph Explorer.
Sign in using your Azure credentials to run the Graph Explorer against your tenant.
See image.
Under Authentication, click modify permissions.
See image.
The Modify Permissions window appears.
Select the following permissions from the list, then click Modify Permissions:
Directory.AccessAsUser.All
Directory.Read.All
Directory.ReadWrite.All
See image.
Choose beta for the version.
See image.
Enter the following query to retrieve the list of servicePrincipals from your tenant:
https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals
Click Run Query.
See image.
Under Response Preview, search for the following service principal.
"appDisplayName": "Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)"
The following is a part of the response preview for the Private Access application. Its id is highlighted in green.
{ "id": "c7195233-3226-4121-b436-b8e755bab66c", "deletedDateTime": null, "accountEnabled": true, "addIns": [], "appDisplayName": "Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)",
Use the id to enter the following query:
https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals/<"id" of ZPA application>
In this example, it's https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals/c7195233-3226-4121-b436-b8e755bab66c.
Click Run Query.
See image.
You will get a response preview similar to the following. The appRoles property is highlighted in green.

{ "@odata.context": "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/$metadata#servicePrincipals/$entity", "id": "c7195233-3226-4121-b436-b8e755bab66c", "deletedDateTime": null, "accountEnabled": true, "addIns": [], "appDisplayName": "Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)", "appId": "6a59ce75-7dd0-4033-a651-8053a9884f88", "appOwnerOrganizationId": "6f7ada54-20ef-4a88-810b-a1c4179e8da9", "appRoleAssignmentRequired": false, "appRoles": [ { "allowedMemberTypes": [ "User" ], "description": "msiam_access", "displayName": "msiam_access", "id": "8866de6e-6d1e-4990-b534-2927284b7c14", "isEnabled": true, "origin": "Application", "value": null } ],
Copy the entire appRoles property and paste it in the Request Body.
See image.
Add roles in the same JSON format. Each role must:
Be in the same format as the msiam_access role
Have a unique id (e.g., "id": "82811e87-6f98-4510-95e5-9cbe849acfad"). You can use a Globally Unique Identifier (GUID) generator.
Have ServicePrincipal as the origin (e.g., "origin": "ServicePrincipal")
Have a unique value (e.g., "value": "Engineer")
In the following request body example, the Engineer and Quality_Assurance roles are being added:

{ "appRoles": [ { "allowedMemberTypes": [ "User" ], "description": "msiam_access", "displayName": "msiam_access", "id": "8866de6e-6d1e-4990-b534-2927284b7c14", "isEnabled": true, "origin": "Application", "value": null }, { "allowedMemberTypes": [ "User" ], "description": "Engineer", "displayName": "Engineer", "id": "8866de6e-6d1e-4990-b534-2927284b7c15", "isEnabled": true, "origin": "ServicePrincipal", "value": "Engineer" }, { "allowedMemberTypes": [ "User" ], "description": "Quality_Assurance", "displayName": "Quality_Assurance", "id": "8866de6e-6d1e-4990-b534-2927284b7c16", "isEnabled": true, "origin": "ServicePrincipal", "value": "Quality_Assurance" } ], }
Choose PATCH.
See image.
Click Run Query. If your request body patched successfully, you'll see a success status code.
See image.

To see if the roles were added, under History on the left navigation pane, choose the query with the "id" of the Private Access application. In this example, it's https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals/c7195233-3226-4121-b436-b8e755bab66c.
See image.

Under Response Preview, scroll down to the appRoles property, and you'll see the added roles. In this example, within the section highlighted in green, the added roles are Quality_ Assurance and Engineer:

{ "@odata.context": "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/$metadata#servicePrincipals/$entity", "id": "c7195233-3226-4121-b436-b8e755bab66c", "deletedDateTime": null, "accountEnabled": true, "addIns": [], "appDisplayName": "Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)", "appId": "6a59ce75-7dd0-4033-a651-8053a9884f88", "appOwnerOrganizationId": "6f7ada54-20ef-4a88-810b-a1c4179e8da9", "appRoleAssignmentRequired": false, "appRoles": [ { "allowedMemberTypes": [ "User" ], "description": "msiam_access", "displayName": "msiam_access", "id": "8866de6e-6d1e-4990-b534-2927284b7c14", "isEnabled": true, "origin": "Application", "value": null }, { "allowedMemberTypes": [ "User" ], "description": "Quality_Assurance", "displayName": "Quality_Assurance", "id": "8866de6e-6d1e-4990-b534-2927284b7c16", "isEnabled": true, "origin": "ServicePrincipal", "value": "Quality_Assurance" }, { "allowedMemberTypes": [ "User" ], "description": "Engineer", "displayName": "Engineer", "id": "8866de6e-6d1e-4990-b534-2927284b7c15", "isEnabled": true, "origin": "ServicePrincipal", "value": "Engineer" } ], "displayName": "Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)", "errorUrl": null, "homepage": "https://samlsp.private.zscaler.com/auth/sso?metadata=zscalerprivateaccess|ISV9.2|primary|z", "keyCredentials": [
You need the roles you added in order to complete step f of the Assigning Roles to Groups procedure.
2. Assigning Roles to Groups
Assign roles to the groups in the Private Access application. Each group must be paired with its own role (i.e., 1:1 mapping ratio between groups and roles).
To assign a role to a group:
Log in to the Azure portal and go to Azure Active Directory > Enterprise applications from the left navigation pane.
See image.
Click All applications, then click the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) application you added for the Adding Roles in the Private Access Application procedure.
See image.
Click Users and groups, then click Add user.
See image.
In the Add Assignment panel that appears, select Users and groups.
See image.
Select the group you want to assign a role to (e.g., the Engineer group), then click Select.
See image.
Click Select Role, then choose the role you added for the Adding Roles in the Private Access Application procedure (e.g., the Engineer role).
See image.
Click Select.
In the Add Assignment panel, click Assign.
See image.
Repeat this procedure for each role you added for the Adding Roles in the Private Access Application procedure.
3. Importing the memberOf Attribute
You must import the memberOf attribute to Private Access. Ensure that you have already added the attribute in Azure.
To import the memberOf attribute to Private Access:
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Administration > Identity > Private Access > IDP Configuration.
On the IdP Configuration page, expand the user SSO configuration for Azure AD.
Click Import SAML Attributes.
If Private Access was correctly configured, the link redirects you to the SSO login page.
Sign in using your Azure AD credentials. The Private Access authentication service automatically imports the memberOf attribute.
Click Save.

blocks.text: After configuring your IdP, be sure to verify the configuration.
If you are verifying your Private Access admin SSO configuration, you can also go to myapps.microsoft.com. From your Dashboard, click on the Zscaler Private Access app to initiate admin SSO.
